title: A Oath for the Thorn
premise: Zephyrine Sandoval has kept the Thorn Gate sealed for twelve years, selling harmless charms in a city where magic is a hanging offense. When a mute child arrives speaking the First Tongue — the language of the realm beyond the gate — Zephyrine learns the covenant binding both worlds is unraveling, and the child is its living key. Hunted by the city's witch-finders and pursued by exiles from the other side who want the gate thrown open, Zephyrine must gather the scattered oath-keepers who once bound it: his old found family, broken by betrayal and grief. In the end, Zephyrine reforges the covenant not with power but by surrendering his own memories of belonging, choosing to become the gate's new anchor — while the found family he rebuilt chooses to stay beside him, remembering what he no longer can.
about_author: Juniper Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters between estranged siblings before turning to fiction. She writes about doors, debts, and the families we build when the old ones fail us.

chapters.title: The Boy at the Door
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. On a rain-lashed night, a silent boy appears at Zephyrine's charm shop, speaking words that make the wards on the Thorn Gate hum in answer. Zephyrine hides him from a passing patrol, feeling the first crack in twelve years of careful numbness. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness awakening old fear.

chapters.title: Charms for a Lawless City
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A day in the shop shows how Zephyrine survives: small charms with the magic sanded off, sold to neighbors who half-suspect and half-protect him. The boy, whom he names Wren, watches everything hungrily. A witch-finder's notice appears on the corner post. Emotional beat: the fragile peace of hiding.

chapters.title: What the Gate Remembers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine descends to the Thorn Gate beneath the shop and finds its seal scarred — someone has been chipping at it for months. Wren touches the stone and speaks fluently in the First Tongue, and the gate answers with a vision: a moon counting down thirteen turns. Emotional beat: dread replacing denial.

chapters.title: The Witch-Finder's Visit
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Inspector Corvane Hale visits under pretense of licensing, probing about 'unregistered children.' Zephyrine lies well but notices Hale's iron cuff — witch-finder gear disguised as a watchman's badge. Afterward, Wren speaks his first common word: 'thirteen.' Emotional beat: hunted, and out of time.

chapters.title: A Name Cut in Two
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, rendered as impressionistic near-silence. Through Wren's eyes we see the other realm: a sky like torn silk, and the memory of being sent through the gate by a woman who called him 'key' and wept. He does not understand why he was chosen, only that going back means dying. Emotional beat: loneliness mirrored across two worlds.

chapters.title: The Exile at the Market
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A stranger named Sable Vane recognizes the First Tongue on Wren's lips and offers help — then reveals she crossed over before the gate closed and wants it reopened, whatever the cost. Zephyrine refuses; she leaves a warning: others are coming who won't ask. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Twelve Years Ago
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, flashback chapter. The night the covenant broke: Zephyrine's found family of five oath-keepers argued over whether to seal the gate or share it, and a betrayal — by Zephyrine himself, who acted alone — sealed it with blood. One keeper died; the rest scattered. Emotional beat: guilt as the story's buried engine.

chapters.title: Finding Odile
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine tracks the first surviving oath-keeper, Odile Ferran, now a lighthouse keeper three days north. She greets him with a slap, then a hug, then fury — but when she sees Wren, her anger collapses into awe. She agrees to come, bringing an oath-stone fragment. Emotional beat: forgiveness offered but not yet earned.

chapters.title: Hale Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Corvane Hale's POV. Hale's chapters reveal the witch-finders' true doctrine: they don't fear magic, they covet it, harvesting it through the iron cuffs. Hale suspects the charm-shop keeper and sets a trap using a staged raid on a neighbor. Emotional beat: cold ambition; the law as predator.

chapters.title: The Neighbor's Sacrifice
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The trap springs: Zephyrine's neighbor Tam takes the fall for harboring Wren and is arrested. Zephyrine must choose — flee with Wren or stay and burn his cover to testify. He testifies, revealing himself, and escapes in the chaos Odile engineers. Emotional beat: the cost of belonging, paid forward.

chapters.title: Road of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Zephyrine, Wren, and Odile travel toward the second keeper, sheltered by strangers the trio once helped with 'harmless' charms. Each kindness repaid deepens the theme: the family you make is built transaction by transaction until it becomes love. Wren begins speaking common words. Emotional beat: warmth gathering against the cold.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sable Vane's POV. Sable intercepts the travelers and reveals the exiles' plight: the far realm is dying, its magic bleeding through the damaged gate, and reopening it is survival. She offers Zephyrine truth instead of threat — including the name of the betrayer's victim. Emotional beat: enemy reframed as grieving kin.

chapters.title: The Keeper Who Died
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. At a mountain shrine they find the fifth keeper, Merrin — not dead, as Zephyrine believed, but bound inside the gate itself as its failing anchor, alive and aware for twelve years. Merrin's mind is fraying; the covenant breaks fully when the thirteenth moon turns unless a new anchor replaces them. Emotional beat: horror and heartbreak entwined.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren understands at last why he was sent: children born of both realms can hold the covenant without dissolving into it — but holding it will still take his childhood, his voice, his self. He decides, silently, that he would rather give himself than let Zephyrine do it. Emotional beat: sacrificial love learned too young.

chapters.title: Iron at the Gate
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Hale, having harvested enough magic to crack the seal himself, leads the witch-finders to the Thorn Gate, intending to own both realms. Sable's exiles arrive from the other side simultaneously. Three armies of want converge on one door. Emotional beat: collision course.

chapters.title: The Betrayal Repeated
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Cornered, Zephyrine almost repeats his original sin — acting alone, sealing the gate with blood to end the crisis. Odile stops him with the words he needed twelve years ago: 'Not without us. Never again without us.' The found family formally reforms around the broken covenant. Emotional beat: the thematic hinge — shared burden over solitary sacrifice.

chapters.title: Storm of Iron and Silk
chapters.summary: Climax, part one. Battle at the gate: witch-finders against exiles while the covenant fails overhead, the thirteenth moon rising cracked and red. Hale breaches the inner chamber; Merrin's anchor shatters. Wren steps into the anchor-stone's place before anyone can stop him. Emotional beat: everything breaking at once.

chapters.title: The Oath Reforged
chapters.summary: Climax, part two. Zephyrine pulls Wren free and takes the anchor himself — but instead of sealing alone, he speaks the covenant as an open oath, with Odile, Sable, Merrin's remnant, and even reformed terms for the exiles bound to it. Shared anchoring dilutes the cost. Hale, touching the living covenant, is consumed by the magic he tried to hoard. Emotional beat: triumph through communion, not conquest.

chapters.title: What Was Given
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The price comes due: Zephyrine's memories of his found family dissolve into the gate — their names, their faces, twelve years of belonging. He wakes knowing only that the people weeping around him are his, though he cannot say why. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude in the same breath.

chapters.title: Two Doors, One House
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The aftermath: the gate stands open but governed, a border rather than a wound. Sable becomes the far side's envoy; Odile and Merrin's remnant rebuild the shrine; Wren, whole and voiced, refuses to be a key ever again. The city's law bends slowly toward tolerance. Emotional beat: cautious, hard-won hope.

chapters.title: Learning Him Again
chapters.summary: Odile and Wren's alternating POV. The found family gently reintroduces Zephyrine to himself — letters he wrote, charms he made, the story of the boy at the door. When Zephyrine laughs at a joke he doesn't remember making, something mends that memory alone couldn't reach. Emotional beat: love persisting past forgetting.

chapters.title: An Oath for the Thorn
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, final chapter. On the anniversary, the family gathers at the gate, and Zephyrine — keeper again, by choice this time — adds a new line to the covenant: that no one shall anchor it alone. Wren takes his hand. The thirteenth moon sets whole. Emotional beat: belonging chosen anew, every day.
